issues.failure_explanation: The quantity (a_u-a_l)/2 is half the interval width, which is less than eps. It is not an estimate of a, so |a - a_hat| < eps does not follow from a lying in [a_l,a_u] with width < 2 eps. For example, a = 0.5 gives a_hat close to 0. The correct estimator is the midpoint (a_u+a_l)/2. The same formula is used in line 7 of Algorithm 1 and in Theorem main theorem.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the estimator by the midpoint (a_u+a_l)/2 in Proposition m-IQAE and Algorithm 1. The rest of the analysis is unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: As written, the estimator and the algorithm's output do not satisfy the stated accuracy guarantee. The statement is not literally true.
issues.title: Amplitude estimator defined as half-width instead of midpoint
issues.why_classification: This is a one-line local correction that preserves all claims and bounds.

issues.failure_explanation: Since X R_y(a) X = R_y(-a), the circuit with two copies of R_y(theta/2) gives R_y(theta) when the control is 0 and the identity when the control is 1. This is the opposite of the claimed controlled rotation. One of the two rotations must be R_y(-theta/2), and likewise for R_x. The stated gate count of 2 rotations plus 2 CNOTs is unaffected.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Use R_y(theta/2) CNOT R_y(-theta/2) CNOT, and similarly for R_x. The elementary gate counts are unchanged.
issues.overall_effect: The construction as written does not implement the claimed gate, so the payoff-rotation circuit (Lemma quantum linear rotation) and the C^n(X) gate count in Proposition m-IQAE rest on an incorrect circuit identity. The gate-count claims survive after correction.
